age.evidence: Male Wistar-Han rats (Charles River, Sulzfeld, Germany) weighting from 280 to 350 g (age of 120-180 PND) were used in all performed experiments.

sex.evidence: Male Wistar-Han rats (Charles River, Sulzfeld, Germany) ... were used in all performed experiments.

dosing.evidence: During the experiment animals received subcutaneous (sc) single injections of 25B-NBOMe dissolved in 0.9% NaCl at five doses of 0.1, 0.3, 1, 3, and 10 mg/kg.
LSD was injected ip at a dose of 0.1 mg/kg.
Scopolamine dissolved in 0.9% NaCl was injected ip at the dose of 1 mg/kg 5 min before administration of 25B-NBOMe.

group_housing.evidence: The animals were initially acclimatized and housed (5 per cage) in environmentally controlled rooms

day_night_flipped.evidence: under 12-h light/dark cycle (the light was switched on at 6 a.m.)

assays.assay_name: Wet Dog Shake (Head and Body Shakes) Test
assays.assay_description: Head and body twitches (WDS) counted by a blinded observer immediately after injection over a 240-min observation period (12 observation periods summed); 25B-NBOMe 0.1–10 mg/kg s.c. and LSD 0.1 mg/kg i.p. as reference.

application_type.evidence: 25B-NBOMe subcutaneous (sc) injections; LSD was injected ip at a dose of 0.1 mg/kg (LSD tested as reference in WDS, Fig. 5).

setup_restrain.evidence: Behaviour ... was counted immediately after drug injection during 240-min observation period by an experienced observer; no restraint described.

food_restriction.evidence: Observation apparatus not described; no food mentioned during observation.

water_restriction.evidence: Observation apparatus not described; no water mentioned during observation.

time_to_assay.evidence: counted immediately after drug injection during 240-min observation period

sample_size.evidence: n = 8 per experimental group (Fig. 5); F6,49 indicates 7 groups (control, 5 doses 25B-NBOMe, LSD)

outcomes.summary: 25B-NBOMe induced head and body twitches at all doses with an inverted U-shaped dose-response; 0.3 mg/kg was most potent and other doses weaker but significant. LSD (0.1 mg/kg) was nearly as potent as the highest 25B-NBOMe dose.
outcomes.evidence: 25B-NBOMe induced head and body twitches (WDS) in rats, which were observed immediately after the administration. The dose of 0.3 mg/kg produced the most potent effect (Fig. 5). The effect of 0.1, 1, 3, and 10 mg/kg doses was weaker but significant (F6,49 = 127, p < 0.0001).

B1_num_measures.evidence: Scores were summed and totaled from 12 observation periods. Results were expressed as an average of sum values of all episodes during the observation time.

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: Scores were summed and totaled from 12 observation periods; no time-course reported.

B3_sequential_structure.evidence: No sequence or transition analysis reported.

B4_ethological.evidence: WDS/HTR is excluded from ethological behaviours per rubric.

B5_social.evidence: Assay does not target social behaviour.

B7_automated_classification.evidence: counted ... by an experienced observer who was blind to the treatments

B8_multivariate.evidence: One-way ANOVA followed by Tukey's post hoc test.

D3_recording_days.evidence: counted immediately after drug injection during 240-min observation period

assays.assay_description: Wooden square arena (60×60×40 cm), familiarization 24 h before; introductory (two identical objects) and recognition (one novel object) sessions of 5 min each with 30-min interval, introductory session 20 min after injection. Novel/familiar exploration time and recognition index (Ri) reported for recognition session. 25B-NBOMe 0.3 and 3 mg/kg, with/without scopolamine pretreatment.

application_type.evidence: we evaluated the effect of the two doses of 25B-NBOMe (0.3 and 3 mg/kg, sc) (scopolamine, non-psychedelic, given ip)

setup_habituation.evidence: Each animal was familiarized with the arena (pre-test, without any object) 24 h before the testing day.

setup_restrain.evidence: Free exploration of objects in an open arena; no restraint described.

food_restriction.evidence: No food present in the arena (standard apparatus).

water_restriction.evidence: No water present in the arena (standard apparatus).

time_to_assay.evidence: The introductory session was performed 20 min after injection of a drug

sample_size.evidence: n = 6-10 per experimental group (Fig. 6); n = 6-12 per experimental group (Fig. 7)

outcomes.summary: 25B-NBOMe 3 mg/kg, but not 0.3 mg/kg, lowered the recognition index (Ri ~45% vs ~72% control) and abolished novel-object preference, indicating impaired short-term recognition memory. Scopolamine reversed the 25B-NBOMe-induced decrease in Ri.
outcomes.statistics: Exploration time F(2,23)=278, p<0.0001; Ri F(2,23)=139, p<0.0001; scopolamine experiment: novel exploration F(3,27)=40, p<0.0001; Ri F(3,27)=18, p<0.01
outcomes.evidence: There was a significant difference in the Ri between animals treated with the higher dose of 25B-NBOMe and the control group (Fig. 6b; F2,23 = 139, p < 0.0001). Importantly, the Ri in the control and low-dose 25B-NBOMe-treated group reached ca. 72% and 68%, respectively, while in the 25B-NBOMe 3 mg/kg group, it was 45%.

B1_num_measures.evidence: Exploration time in the recognition session for the familiar (A) and novel object (B); Ri

B4_ethological.evidence: Exploration of an object was defined as follows: licking, sniffing, or touching the object

B6_cognitive.evidence: cognitive functions were examined with the novel object recognition test (NOR)

B7_automated_classification.evidence: Exploration time was measured using a digital laboratory timer by two independent observers blind to the experimental design.

B8_multivariate.evidence: One-way ANOVA and t tests only.

E1_environment_type.evidence: wooden closed square arena with painted black walls (60 × 60 × 40 cm)

E2_shelter.evidence: Open arena with two objects; no shelter described.

E5_enrichment.evidence: Objects (black metal can, green vase) are test stimuli, not enrichment.

E7_social_context.evidence: Each animal was tested individually in the arena.

E8_food_water.evidence: No food or water described in arena.

D1_continuity.evidence: Ri ... calculated ... for results obtained during recognition session; only recognition-session data are reported.

D2_session_duration.evidence: introductory and recognition one (5 min each)

D3_recording_days.evidence: Familiarization 24 h before was without data collection; test sessions on the testing day only.

D4_baseline.evidence: familiarized with the arena (pre-test, without any object) 24 h before — habituation without reported data.

assays.assay_description: Round black arena (1 m diameter, virtually divided into 8 sections), rats placed 30 min after s.c. 25B-NBOMe (0.3, 3 mg/kg; with/without scopolamine) and recorded for 10 min; walking time, line crossings, peeping, grooming and rearing scored.

application_type.evidence: Rats were placed in the middle of the arena 30 min after 25B-NBOMe subcutaneous injection (scopolamine, non-psychedelic, ip)

setup_restrain.evidence: Rats were placed in the middle of the arena ... and their behavior was recorded for 10 min.

food_restriction.evidence: No food in open-field arena (standard apparatus).

water_restriction.evidence: No water in open-field arena (standard apparatus).

time_to_assay.evidence: Rats were placed in the middle of the arena 30 min after 25B-NBOMe subcutaneous injection

sample_size.evidence: n = 6-10 per experimental group (Fig. 6); n = 6-12 per experimental group (Fig. 7)

outcomes.summary: 25B-NBOMe dose-dependently decreased walking time, line crossings and peeping; no rearing or grooming was observed in treated rats. Scopolamine increased walking and crossing vs. control but did not prevent the 25B-NBOMe-induced decreases.
outcomes.statistics: Walking F(2,19)=134, p<0.0001; crossing F(2,19)=110, p<0.0001; peeping F(2,19)=32, p<0.0001; scopolamine experiment: walking F(3,23)=213, crossing F(3,23)=164, peeping F(3,23)=68, all p<0.0001
outcomes.evidence: 25B-NBOMe decreased the time of walking (F2,19 = 134, p < 0.0001) and the number of episodes of crossing (F2,19 = 110, p < 0.0001) and peeping (F2,19 = 32, p < 0.0001) in a dose-dependent manner (Fig. 6c). No episodes of rearing and grooming were observed in animals treated with both doses of 25B-NBOMe (data not shown).

B1_num_measures.evidence: time of walking, number of line crossings, episodes of peeping under the arena, number of events of grooming, and number of rearings

B4_ethological.evidence: episodes of peeping under the arena, number of events of grooming, and number of rearings

E1_environment_type.evidence: A round black arena (1 m in diameter) was used

E6_spatial.evidence: virtually divided into 8 sections of the wheel

E7_social_context.evidence: Rats were placed in the middle of the arena individually.

D1_continuity.evidence: their behavior was recorded for 10 min

assays.assay_description: Med Associates Seamless Open Field Arenas (43×43×30 cm) with dark insert dividing into light and dark compartments; rat placed in dark compartment 20 min after s.c. 25B-NBOMe (0.3, 3 mg/kg), 15-min free exploration; time in each compartment, ambulatory distance, vertical, stereotypical activity and immobility recorded via infrared beams.

application_type.evidence: two doses of 25B-NBOMe (0.3 and 3 mg/kg, sc); The rat was placed in the dark compartment 20 min after injection of a drug

setup_restrain.evidence: A hole in the insert enabled rats to move freely between compartments ... was allowed to explore freely for 15 min.

food_restriction.evidence: No food in LDB arena (standard apparatus).

water_restriction.evidence: No water in LDB arena (standard apparatus).

time_to_assay.evidence: The rat was placed in the dark compartment 20 min after injection of a drug

sample_size.evidence: n = 8 per experimental group (Fig. 8); control, 0.3 and 3 mg/kg groups

outcomes.summary: 25B-NBOMe 3 mg/kg increased time in the dark compartment and decreased time in the light compartment vs. control, interpreted as anxiogenic. Both doses decreased ambulatory distance, vertical and stereotypical activity in both zones.
outcomes.statistics: Dark vs light within group: control U=11, 0.3 mg/kg U=6, 3 mg/kg U=0, all p<0.001; dark time 3 mg/kg vs control U=0, p<0.001; light time 3 mg/kg vs control U=0, p<0.001; ambulatory, vertical and stereotypical activity decreased by both doses (U=0–15, p<0.001)
outcomes.evidence: the time was longer and statistically significant in the rats treated with 25B-NBOMe at the dose of 3 mg/kg as compared to control (U = 0, p < 0.001).

B1_num_measures.evidence: The measured parameters included immobility time, ambulatory distance, vertical activity time, stereotypical activity time, and the time spent in the dark and light compartment.

B4_ethological.evidence: Zone time and beam-break activity counts only.

B7_automated_classification.evidence: The data were collected using Med State software (Activity monitor, Med Associates) — beam-break system.

E1_environment_type.evidence: Seamless Open Field Arenas for rats (43 × 43 × 30 cm; Med Associates)

E2_shelter.evidence: A dark insert was used to divide the chamber into two equally sized compartments: a light compartment and a dark compartment.

E6_spatial.evidence: A hole in the insert enabled rats to move freely between compartments.

E7_social_context.evidence: The rat was placed in the dark compartment

D1_continuity.evidence: allowed to explore freely for 15 min

D2_session_duration.evidence: allowed to explore freely for 15 min

judge_notes: All three candidates identified the same four behavioural assays (WDS, NOR, OFT, LDB); microdialysis and comet assay correctly excluded as non-behavioural.
WDS B1 set to score 0 (single measure: WDS count); gemma's score of 1 for a '1' category was inconsistent with the rubric.

WDS application_type set to 'multiple' because the psychedelic LSD (i.p.) was administered alongside s.c. 25B-NBOMe in this assay; for NOR/OFT, scopolamine is not a psychedelic so application_type kept as s.c.

NOR D1/D3/D4 overridden to Single session/1 day/No baseline: the paper reports only recognition-session data ('for results obtained during recognition session'), and the 24-h pre-test was arena familiarization without reported data.
NOR B4 kept as Yes (modal) since object exploration was defined as licking, sniffing or touching; medium confidence.
OFT and LDB B1 scored 4-6 (score 2) per the explicit lists of measured parameters; gemma's '2-3' value label corrected.
MDMA excluded from dosing (used only in non-behavioural comet assay); scopolamine included as a non-psychedelic drug administered in behavioural experiments.
WDS n_total inferred as 56 from 7 groups × n=8 (F6,49); LDB n_total 24 from 3 groups × n=8; NOR/OFT n_total left null due to overlapping cohorts across Fig. 6 and Fig. 7.
